clauses.reason: Section 1(a) requires covered contracts to contain a stipulation forbidding employment of persons serving court-imposed sentences, with the exception for parolees, probationers and the pardoned or released and for work-release inmates of State and other jurisdictions that meet the conditions in item (1) and the Attorney General's certification in item (2). It is operative on 2026-10-14 in amended form. Executive Order 12608 section 23, September 9, 1987 (no separate effective date; signing date used), added the words "the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands," after "American Samoa," wherever they appear in section 1(a) (before: the listed territories ran from Puerto Rico through American Samoa and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands; after: the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands is also listed). Executive Order 12943, December 13, 1994 (signing date used), added subsection 1(c): The provisions of this order do not apply to purchases made under the micropurchase authority contained in section 32 of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act, as amended. The clause continues, amended, as the Code note reproduces.

clauses.reason: Section 2 directs that the procurement regulations (Federal Procurement Regulations, Armed Services Procurement Regulations and comparable agency regulations) be revised to reflect the order's policy. No held source dates a first complete performance: the 1974 revisions are not held. The directive is judged operative because it states a continuing conformity duty that the held record shows being applied again after each amendment (Federal Acquisition Regulation rulemakings of 1994 to 1996 revising the convict-labor clause after Executive Orders 12608 and 12943) and because 48 CFR 22.201 and 52.222-3 still implement the order; this is an inference from those regulations, not a held source that fixes performance or non-performance.

Section 3 supersedes Executive Order 325A. That is a one-time act that took effect with the order; section 4 makes the order effective as of January 1, 1974, so the first end of this clause, the supersession having been performed, is January 1, 1974 (the alternative reading is the signing date, December 29, 1973). The surviving consequence, that Executive Order 325A stays superseded, is a status and not a continuing command of this order.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11755 of December 29, 1973 (39 FR 779) permits Federal contractors to employ non-Federal prison inmates on paid work release when listed conditions are met (section 1), requires the Attorney General to certify, and after notice and hearing to revoke certification of, a jurisdiction's work-release laws (sections 1(a)(2) and 1(b)), directs revision of the procurement regulations (section 2), supersedes Executive Order 325A (section 3) and takes effect January 1, 1974 (section 4). It was issued under the President's own authority; the preamble recited 18 U.S.C. 4082, since replaced, but Executive Order 12943 of December 13, 1994 rewrote that recital to cite 18 U.S.C. 3621 and 3622 and the Bureau of Prisons, so no repealed-statute dependency is left in the order as amended. The held original is an official Federal Register OCR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11755.txt) with irregular letter spacing, so no quotation from it is used. Two held later orders amend it by amendment, not ending: Executive Order 12608 section 23 (September 9, 1987) adds the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands to the territories listed in section 1(a), and Executive Order 12943 (December 13, 1994) rewrites the second preamble paragraph and adds subsection 1(c) excluding micropurchases. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each amended clause continues, amended, with the parent order. The current basis for every operative clause is the held original read with the three bounded searches, whose coverage notes were read. As context only, 28 CFR 0.94-1(b) (eCFR text amended through 2026-10-27, held in the packet as a custody record, so not cited as a source) delegates to the Director of the Bureau of Justice Assistance the Attorney General's power under the order to certify and revoke certification of work-release laws. The searches: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) hit one note, the printed order as amended through Executive Order 12943 under 18 U.S.C. 3622 note; the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) hit eight regulations, including 28 CFR 0.94-1 and the Federal Acquisition Regulation sections that apply the order; the Federal Register disposition catalog search hit the two amendments. No revocation, supersession or own-terms end was found. Section 3 (supersession of Executive Order 325A) was complete when the order took effect.
